01 / THE CLASSIFICATION

Four questions, one code.

The code order is always S → O → R → G。
A shared code indicates coarse-grained similarities, not identical reactions.

∴
What guides this classification?

We describe each key mechanistic event using electronic state, donor–acceptor and frontier orbitals, electron-pair or single-electron movement, and nuclear geometry. SORG is a project-defined educational index, not a validated quantum-mechanical invariant or an IUPAC standard. The O and R boundaries remain open to revision.

Read the assignment rules ↗
READ AN EXAMPLEWhy do SN2 and proton transfer both map to 1122?

Both are closed-shell donor–acceptor events. One bond is replaced by another as approach and departure are coupled. The reaction center and orbital details belong to the mechanism description.

03 / METHOD & EVIDENCE

Ground each simplification
and make its limits visible.

Describe reactions through electronic state, orbital coupling, electron reorganization, and nuclear motion.
Mechanisms and quantum-chemical data are central; reaction names are the index.

01

One event, one code

Code distinct elementary events separately. Preserve repeated codes: SN1 ionization and capture are both 1111; water as the nucleophile also requires a 1122 deprotonation. Resonance forms and multiple arrows within one event do not add steps.

02

Codes are hypotheses to test

SORG organizes reactions by electronic state, orbital interactions, bond reorganization, and geometry. It is an educational approximation, not a validated quantum-mechanical invariant or IUPAC standard. A shared code cannot replace molecular-orbital or electronic-structure data.

03

Quantum data require a method

Orbital coupling, orbital gaps, electron density, bond order, and geometry depend on the molecule, conformation, electronic state, solvent model, basis set, and method. Numerical values require traceable literature or reproducible calculations; qualitative arrows are not ab initio results.

Sources and content notes ＋

Each entry cites mechanism sources. References support the mechanism and chemical evidence; they do not endorse SORG codes. The mechanism panel includes full reaction schemes, intermediates, sequential steps, and image credits. Textual educational content is provided under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Access for free at OpenStax Organic Chemistry · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

Current scope

The atlas focuses on foundational polar reactions, radical-chain events, and thermal pericyclic reactions. Excited-state S3 and O4/R4 electron-transfer cases remain in the codebook but are not yet assigned. Metal aggregation, explicit solvent participation, and full reaction networks are not yet covered; each entry states its scope.
